title: replay-proxy: lightweight autoreplay diagnostic proxy for on-call and canary replays
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Adds a replay proxy that captures sanitised diagnostic bundles for on-call replays and scheduled canaries. Opt-in by default. No breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: On-call run-throughs and canary experiments frequently need a compact, deterministic replay of production failures without shipping full trace dumps or secrets. This PR adds a lightweight autoreplay diagnostic proxy that records request/response context + bounded telemetry, sanitizes sensitive fields, and exposes a secure replay API for on-call investigators and scheduled canaries.

What this change does: Adds a small sidecar-style proxy and server component (slo-toolkit/diag-proxy) which can run in-process, as a sidecar, or as an ephemeral job. The proxy captures a concise bundle: headers, request body (trimmed to policy size), trace IDs, relevant metrics snapshot, and an annotated call sequence. A sanitizer pipeline removes secrets, PII, and redacts large blobs; an allowlist controls additional keys. Replays run against a pinned sandbox environment with deterministic injection of latency and feature flags to allow safe reproduction.

Design highlights: single-file bundle format (ndjson lines) for incremental upload and streaming; retention and eviction policy configurable via helm values; RBAC-protected replay endpoint (token-scoped) with audit log hooks; integration points for incident-bot to attach replay snapshots to incident cards. The proxy is intentionally small (single binary + python sanitizer module) so it is easy to include in oncall flows and scheduled canaries.

Safety: Default behavior is off. When enabled, proxy strips Authorization, Cookie, and all keys matching regex patterns in config. Sanitizer runs policy checks and fails ingestion if sensitive heuristics exceed thresholds. Replays are forced into a sandbox network namespace and use mock dependencies unless explicitly flagged for internal-only debugging.

Testing & rollout plan: Unit tests and replay harness included; e2e canary job added to ci/ to run a synthetic failure and verify replay and sanitizer. Rollout will start as an opt-in helm value in staging, followed by an invitation-only beta with SRE, then gradual enablement for on-call canary runs.

Related: ENG-7421 (diagnostic portability), SRE-1983 (oncall replay ergonomics), SUP-4012 (support case requesting replay snapshots).
